name: level1-playthrough-revolt
description: Level 1 worker revolt scenario: aggressive krackle blasts, no well-being buildings, long tick cycles with events to trigger worker rebellion

steps.description: #553: staffed:true hires and equips, for free, employee #1 driller (blasting lvl1, driving.drill_rig lvl1) through #5 driver, plus vehicles #1 drill_rig through #4 rock_fragmenter (all unmanned). Cost is free -- does not change starting cash. The file's own 7 hand-hired employees below become #6-#12.

#553: staffed:true does NOT auto-assign a driver -- the free drill_rig (vehicle #1) is still a mesh nobody can drive until employee #1, the only qualified driller on the roster at this point, boards it. The assign row's <select> defaults to its only eligible option (employee #1 is the sole driving.drill_rig holder here), so the plain assign click resolves to them without needing to pick an option.

#553 sandbox-measured finding: staffed:true parks its 4 vehicles in a row at (0,2)/(2,2)/(4,2)/(6,2), and on dusty_hollow's terrain that row sits inside the map's only ramp corridor out of the spawn corner -- tickVehicleOnNavGrid recomputes the same A* path every tick (avoidVehicles:false) and only refuses the immediate next cell if another vehicle already occupies it (isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle), so the drill_rig (vehicle #1) advances exactly one cell to (1,2) and then waits forever behind the unmanned debris_hauler parked at (2,2) -- confirmed by direct trace: 40+ ticks stuck at (1,2), waitingTicks climbing, holeCount never leaving 0. This file never uses a debris_hauler, rock_digger or rock_fragmenter (zero hauling/fragment-breaking anywhere in its script), so scrapping the blocker -- and the other two idle vehicles that would otherwise just draw maintenance upkeep for nothing -- clears the corridor and turns dead weight into cash.
rock_digger #3 was never in the drill_rig's path, but this file has no use for it either -- scrapped for the same reason as #2: pure upkeep with nothing to show for it.

rock_fragmenter #4, same reasoning. Sandbox-measured residual proceeds across all three scraps ($10,000 + $20,000 + $12,800 = $42,800) fund the 7 hires below without touching the $50,000 opening balance.
#553: this and the following 6 hires are the file's own original crew, renumbered #6-#12 now that staffed:true claims #1-#5 first.

#553: employee #7. Deliberately left unlicensed for driving.drill_rig -- sandbox-measured, licensing this driller as a backup only adds a second casualty to blast 1 (they end up standing near the pattern too) without changing the outcome, since patterns 2-4 stall on the missing vehicle regardless of how many licensed drillers are left alive (see the note on the pattern-2 drill_plan step below).

expect.note: #596/#597-followup: this 168-tick request completes in full (sandbox-measured: 175->343, all 168 ticks) -- tickCount converted equals->changedBy (issue #596) since the batch running to completion, not a specific running total, is this step's own point. safety drops to a plain 50 (was 56.6): the earlier event is now union_unlucky_days, which carries no safety delta, so there is no tremor bump left to decay from. Along the way, 12 employees' payroll with zero income anywhere in this file crosses the $5,000 threshold and BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100 (Bankruptcy.ts) completes at tick 209 -- bankruptcy fires mid-drill, well before this pattern finishes, let alone blasts. Confirmed via __probeSelector that this is not a race that a longer wait fixes: right now the blast report's own Close button reads "hidden" (still inside its 3s delay); left running past that delay it flips to "covered" -- LevelEndScreen's z-index 9999 sits above BlastReportModal's shared z-index 600 (unlike the event dialog's own 10500, styles.ts), so once armed, the report can never be dismissed post-bankruptcy either, and the event stays gated behind it permanently. `blocked` proves the report's Close button (the real control standing between the player and this event) while `event choose 0` still runs directly to keep wellBeing on the same track as the rest of the file.

Ecology/nuisance stay dropped -- both inherit the real-time-accrual drift from before tick 293 (waitForTutorialStep/waitForSelector polls, see the tick-298 step's note), since they accumulate from a slightly-wrong base rather than from anything decided at any one tick. safety/wellBeing stay exact -- both are floored at 0 by this point, immune to base drift.

#553: this file's premise holds both ways at once. Drilling is real, queued, vehicle-gated work: a single driller sinks the 4x4 pattern (interrupted once by a real random event, union_unlucky_days as of #596/#597 -- not the pre-#596 weather_minor_tremor -- at tick 175, not the pre-#596 tick 125) by tick 343, and 12 employees' payroll with zero income anywhere in this file crosses the bankruptcy threshold before that pattern even finishes drilling (BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100 completes at tick 209, per Bankruptcy.ts) -- levelEndReason is 'bankruptcy' because that fires first, same conclusion as before. But pattern 1's blast, once it finally lands, is catastrophic enough (16 holes x 8kg krackle, CATASTROPHIC rating, 90.3m throw) to kill all 5 staffed employees and destroy the only drill_rig this file ever owns -- and with no vehicle, no licensed spare worth the risk, and cash already deep in the negative, patterns 2-4 order 65 more holes that can never be drilled. The survivors' well-being, pinned at 0 by fatigue collapse with no living quarters anywhere in this file, stays there long enough (REVOLT_TICKS=120, WorkerRevolt.ts) that revolted flips true too -- now at tick 416 (#596/#597: the second random event, politics_competitor_mine, carries no wellBeing delta, so unlike the old union_rep_secretary draw there is no tick-315 bump left to reset the revolt streak, and it completes earlier than the pre-#596/#597 file's tick 445) -- the workforce actually revolts this time, well after the mine is already bankrupt.
